messages:
Alex T: FYI MonarchPay just escalated — after the 08:00 rollout to rerank-v3.0 they see the same queries returning different rerank scores (and some rank flips). They started re-running locally and hit a 400 candidate_count_exceeds_limit error when they tried to send all candidates. Can ML/oncall triage?

Alex T: Repro payload they used (trimmed):
```json
{
  "query": "refund failed transaction  invoice 12345",
  "candidates": ["line item 1 text...", "line item 2 text...", "..."],
  "top_k": 10
}
```

Alex T: Old prod (v2.9) scores (example):
- cand_42: 0.812
- cand_07: 0.605
- cand_99: 0.442

Alex T: New prod (v3.0) scores (same input):
- cand_42: 0.673  <-- dropped
- cand_07: 0.821  <-- jumped above cand_42
- cand_99: 0.438

rerank-bot: Deploy note: rerank-v3.0 rolled to prod at 1719007600 by jenkins-deploy (release: fast-rollout). :rocket:

Maria G: Thanks Alex. Do we know whether MonarchPay is hitting our default route (un-pinned) or explicitly requesting a model?

Alex T: They did not pin — they call the /rerank endpoint with no model param (default route). They only started troubleshooting after noticing customer-facing ranking changes.

Jason L: I'm on it. Quick checklist: (1) can we reproduce locally using the same candidate set and both model versions? (2) compare tokenization/token counts, (3) check whether embed generation changed (online vs precomputed), (4) confirm candidate truncation due to token limits.

Jason L: Try this client command to force v2.9 vs v3.0 and inline embeddings so we isolate embedding drift:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rerank-v2.9","inline_embeddings":true,"query":"refund failed transaction invoice 12345","candidates":["...full candidate 1...","...full candidate 2...", ...]}'
```

Priya N (oncall): A few things to check — small score deltas can be from quantization/float-path changes, but flips like cand_07 overtaking cand_42 look larger. Also confirm we didn’t change similarity metric (cosine -> dot) in v3.0. Any change in precompute/online embedding logic?

Alex T: Also saw this error in their logs when they attempted to resend everything:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"candidate_count_exceeds_limit","detail":"max candidates per request is 100; received 120"}
```

Alex T: They said historically they've sent 120 candidates and relied on the server to accept & truncate, but v3.0 now rejects above-100. We need to confirm whether that behavior changed or if a config was tightened during rollout.

Maria G: That explains the 400s. If v2.9 silently truncated and v3.0 enforces a hard limit, that could change which candidates are considered and thus the final ranks. Was the silent truncation intentional before?

Jason L: Good catch. If candidates are dropped, the pool changes — big impact. I'll reproduce two flows: (A) explicit truncation to first 100, (B) server-side rejection. Also will compare embeddings for the removed candidates to see if any were previously influential (high similarity).

Jason L: Running quick local diff now. Early result: With inline_embeddings + v2.9 I get cand_42 score 0.813. With inline_embeddings + v3.0 but limiting to first 100, cand_42 -> 0.675 (matching reported). So looks like either the scoring model changed OR some candidate texts are being token-truncated differently producing different embeddings.

Priya N (oncall): Action items we should do immediately:
- Confirm whether the default route for un-pinned requests changed policy between v2.9->v3.0 (silent truncation vs hard reject).
- Pin MonarchPay's traffic to rerank-v2.9 until we understand.
- Send repro job to staging with full 120-candidate set and both versions.
- If it is a candidate handling change, file infra rollback or compatibility patch.

Alex T: MonarchPay approved temporary pin to v2.9 until tomorrow. I'll apply and confirm. Ticketing: CS-9142 opened for customer comms and rollback authorization.

Maria G: Also add a note to changelog: breaking change in candidate limit behavior and any default model routing semantics. This needs clear docs.

Jason L: Follow-up: I found that v3.0 introduced a new tokenizer update to better handle punctuation which changes token counts for long candidate items. For some candidates this caused token length > token_limit -> we truncate the tail during embedding prep. That truncation altered embeddings enough to flip scores.

Jason L: Proposed fixes: (1) revert tokenizer change in v3.0 for rerank route, (2) or restore server-side tolerant behavior (accept >100 and truncate client-side with warning), (3) longer term — return a deterministic warning in response body about which candidates were truncated/dropped.

Priya N (oncall): Please escalate decision to runtime/infra for immediate rollback option. I will open an incident and request rollback window.

Alex T: I'll message MonarchPay that we pinned them to v2.9 and that we're investigating tokenizer/truncation behavior; we'll update by EOD. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Maria G: Great — Jason, please paste the staging repro results and raw diffs here when ready. Alex, keep CS updated and paste the incident/rollback link.

Jason L: Will post diffs in this thread — starting long-run batch now (staging).

rerank-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-711 (candidate-handling-regression). Assigned: eng-runtime, led by Jason L.

Alex T: Noted. Closing loop with MonarchPay now.
